title: I Posted the Conservatory Humidity Log After They Propped the Door

parts.text: I read 82 percent at 9:06 a.m. and intern Quill had propped the fern door on a watering can. The plaque said: DOORS LATCHED. LOG HUMIDITY. NO PROPS. I was forty-three, volunteer, holding a clip chart. Quill shrugged. "Interns are the air." I photographed the plaque, the can, and the dropping number. Then I asked for the humidity log. At 9:12 the horticulturist pinged why Quill's name was on a propped door. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The horticulturist can see Quill's watering-can prop on the humidity log.

social.video_title: The intern propped the fern door on a watering can — Part 1/2
social.description: Conservatory, 82 percent, a latched-door plaque. I logged the drop. Would you have asked horticulture?

parts.text: Quill called it airflow until horticulture asked for the still. I printed the log, the plaque, and the photo. The door latched. Quill logged humidity and told the next intern airflow was always about optics. Optics is a word interns use when ferns exist. Door policy now has a second line: CANS ARE NOT LATCHES. I keep the chart. Quill brown-bags the jokes. The house finally looks like a plaque, not a hallway. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.description: Humidity log, latched door, and a second line. Was airflow ever the ferns?
